notes: All regional forms are draft proposals awaiting native content review.
The fixed synthetic benchmark scale is 1000 KRW per source monetary unit; it is not a live exchange rate.
Korean family names precede given names in display; tool fields retain their separate given/family meanings.
Romanized fields represent the same native values, not English translations. English explanations describe meaning and name roles without invented etymology.
The airline network uses 15 Korean and 5 nearby international airports to preserve the original 20 distinct nodes. Routes and schedules are synthetic.
Scenario clock ordering, IDs, reward intent, and frozen task membership remain unchanged.
Airline scope is Korea-centered domestic and nearby international service; the domestic-only source wording must change without adding passport, visa, customs or other new task requirements.

decisions.source_assessment: The English source “Junius Buckminster-Chavel” is harder than same-family Easy sources such as “Lisa Sandoval” and “Michael Santiago”: it has an uncommon first name, a long multi-component surname with a hyphen, and decoys/pronunciation traps at “Chavel/Chaver” and “Junius/Justus.”

hazards.evidence: The caller is instructed to initially say only the given name “경찬,” while the full written answer is “선우 경찬”; the agent must elicit the family name “선우” to recover the full value.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “전체 성함이 어떻게 되나요?” → “선우 경찬입니다. 성은 선우, 이름은 경찬입니다.”

hazards.evidence: “경찬” can be misheard as the decoy “경창” because the final consonant in the second syllable differs, and “선우 경찬” also has the decoy “선우 형찬.”
hazards.resolving_clarification: “이름을 한 글자씩 확인해 주시겠어요?” → “경은 ㄱ의 경, 찬은 ㅊ의 찬입니다. 경찬입니다.”

hazards.evidence: “선우” is a two-syllable family name in “선우 경찬,” unlike common one-syllable family names; the boundary between family name and given name must be captured correctly.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “성이 선이고 이름이 우경찬인가요?” → “아니요, 성이 선우이고 이름이 경찬입니다.”

decisions.source_assessment: The English source “Heyward Golle-Medora” is genuinely harder than the Easy English controls: it contains uncommon name parts, a hyphenated surname, double-letter spelling behavior in “Golle,” and decoys/pronunciation traps such as “Medora/Medart” and “Heyward/Reynard.”

hazards.evidence: The caller initially gives only “지후,” while the full answer is “갈 지후”; the agent must ask for the family name to avoid entering only the given name.

hazards.evidence: The given name “지후” is close to written decoys “지우” and “지호,” so the second syllable “후” may be lost or heard as a neighboring vowel/consonant form.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “지후가 지우인지 지호인지 확인해 주시겠어요?” → “지후입니다. 지, 후 두 글자입니다.”

hazards.evidence: The rare one-syllable family name “갈” in “갈 지후” is not as predictable as common family names like 김/박/이 and may need Hangul confirmation.
hazards.resolving_clarification: “성은 어떤 글자인가요?” → “갈대 할 때 갈, 한 글자 성 갈입니다.”

decisions.comparison_to_easy: Unlike intake_person_names_easy_02 “박민준,” intake_person_names_easy_04 “김지훈,” and intake_person_names_easy_09 “박지은,” where common family names and common given-name syllables are straightforward, “갈 지후” uses the uncommon family name “갈” and close decoys “지후/지우/지호,” creating a real capture hazard beyond the Easy set.

"선우 승겸" is harder because "선우" is a two-syllable surname and "승겸" has close decoys "승검" and "성겸" requiring syllable-level clarification.
